Two-stage analysis of a multi-location augmented p-rep trial

Source: R/augmented_prep_two_stage.R
analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage.Rd

Analyses each location separately (stage 1) and combines the per-location adjusted means across locations (stage 2), weighting them by their precision. This is the approach suggested by Williams, Piepho and Whitaker (2011, Section 3) for adding spatial error components and for heterogeneous error variances across locations: every location gets its own error variance (and, optionally, its own spatial trend), and the stage-2 weights carry that information into the combined means (Möhring and Piepho, 2009).

Usage

analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage(
  data,
  response,
  stage1 = c("blocks", "spatial"),
  weighting = c("full", "diagonal", "none"),
  genotype_by_location = c("random", "none"),
  genotype_col = "all_entries",
  location_col = "location",
  block_col = "block",
  replicate_col = "replicate",
  row_col = "row",
  col_col = "col",
  spatial_nseg = NULL,
  spatial_random_blocks = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A design data frame (usually design$design from augmented_prep_design()), or a design object, with a response column.

response

Name of the numeric response column.

stage1

Stage-1 model: "blocks" or "spatial".

weighting

Stage-2 weighting: "full", "diagonal", or "none".

genotype_by_location

"random" (default) to estimate a genotype-by-location variance in stage 2, or "none" to omit it.

genotype_col, location_col, block_col, replicate_col

Column names, as in analyze_augmented_prep_design().

row_col, col_col

Field row and column coordinate columns, used by stage1 = "spatial".

spatial_nseg

Optional number of P-spline segments for columns and rows, c(col, row). Defaults to half the number of distinct columns and rows of each location (at least 3, at most 40), which is much faster than one segment per row or column and usually as accurate.

spatial_random_blocks

Logical. If TRUE (default), incomplete blocks are included as a random effect in the spatial model.

Value

An object of class augmented_prep_two_stage, a list with

adjusted_means

Combined genotype means ranked best first, with standard errors and the number of locations.

variance_components

Stage-2 REML genotype-by-location variance.

locations

One row per location: stage-1 model, plots, genotypes, residual variance and df, mean SED and, for spatial fits, the effective dimension of the spatial surface.

heterogeneity

Hartley's Fmax ratio of the stage-1 residual variances with a simulated 5% critical value.

stage1_means

The stage-1 genotype means and standard errors per location.

stage1_fits

The stage-1 fits (analysis objects or SpATS objects), named by location.

diagnostics

Settings, number of stage-2 means, REML log-likelihood, mean SED and approximate 5% LSD.

Stage 1

stage1 = "blocks"

The incomplete-block model of analyze_augmented_prep_design() at each location (replicates and blocks fixed, genotypes fixed).

stage1 = "spatial"

A spatial model fitted with the 'SpATS' package (Rodríguez-Álvarez et al., 2018): genotypes fixed, a smooth two-dimensional P-spline surface over the field rows and columns (PSANOVA), replicates fixed and incomplete blocks random. It needs the row and col field coordinates (use field_cols in augmented_prep_design()).

The stage-1 genotype means are BLUEs with their full covariance matrix. Each location needs some error degrees of freedom, i.e. enough p-rep entries for its blocks. In spatial fits part of the plot-to-plot noise is taken up by the smooth surface, so the reported residual variance is somewhat smaller than in the block model; the stage-1 covariance matrix accounts for this, and the Hartley test on spatial residual variances is approximate.

Stage 2

The stage-1 means \(\bar y_{gl}\) are modelled as \(\bar y_{gl} = \mu + \lambda_l + \gamma_g + (\gamma\lambda)_{gl} + e_{gl}\), with fixed locations and genotypes, random genotype-by-location effects with variance \(\sigma^2_{GL}\) (estimated by REML) and stage-1 errors \(e\) whose covariance is taken from stage 1:

weighting = "full"

the full stage-1 covariance matrix of each location (most accurate);

weighting = "diagonal"

only the stage-1 variances (weights \(1 / se^2\));

weighting = "none"

an unweighted analysis of the stage-1 means with a common error, which ignores heterogeneity (for comparison).

Genotype adjusted means average the location effects with equal weights.

References

Williams, E., Piepho, H.-P. and Whitaker, D. (2011). Augmented p-rep designs. Biometrical Journal 53, 19-27. doi:10.1002/bimj.201000102

Möhring, J. and Piepho, H.-P. (2009). Comparison of weighting in two-stage analysis of plant breeding trials. Crop Science 49, 1977-1988. doi:10.2135/cropsci2009.02.0083

Rodríguez-Álvarez, M. X., Boer, M. P., van Eeuwijk, F. A. and Eilers, P. H. C. (2018). Correcting for spatial heterogeneity in plant breeding experiments with P-splines. Spatial Statistics 23, 52-71. doi:10.1016/j.spasta.2017.10.003

See also

analyze_augmented_prep_design() for the one-stage analysis.

Examples

design <- augmented_prep_design(
  treatments = sprintf("G%02d", 1:60),
  locations = c("A", "B", "C"),
  method = "alpha",
  block_size = 6,
  field_cols = 9,
  seed = 1
)
trial <- design$design
set.seed(2)
# Location C is twice as noisy as A and B.
trial$yield <- 50 + stats::rnorm(nrow(trial), sd = ifelse(trial$location == "C", 4, 2))

fit <- analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage(trial, response = "yield")
fit
#> Two-stage augmented p-rep analysis
#> Stage 1: blocks model per location; stage 2: full weighting, genotype x location random
#> 
#> Locations:
#>  location n_plots n_genotypes residual_variance residual_df mean_sed
#>         A      80          60             7.259           7    4.908
#>         B      80          60             2.267           7    2.744
#>         C      80          60            16.970           7    7.338
#> 
#> Hartley Fmax = 7.49 (5% critical value 6.93): error variances differ between locations
#> 
#> Stage-2 variance components:
#>            component variance
#>  genotype x location     1.39
#> 
#> Top adjusted means (60 genotypes):
#>  rank genotype n_locations adjusted_mean std_error
#>     1      G33           3         53.16     1.612
#>     2      G54           3         53.16     1.582
#>     3      G46           3         52.59     1.580
#>     4      G39           3         52.10     1.551
#>     5      G26           3         52.00     1.529
#>     6      G40           3         51.86     1.460
#>     7      G10           3         51.59     1.615
#>     8      G25           3         51.57     1.473
#>     9      G06           3         51.52     1.581
#>    10      G56           3         51.36     1.466
#> Mean SED = 2.162; LSD (5%) = 4.281
fit$locations
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   location stage1_model n_plots n_genotypes residual_variance residual_df
#>   <chr>    <chr>          <int>       <int>             <dbl>       <int>
#> 1 A        blocks            80          60              7.26           7
#> 2 B        blocks            80          60              2.27           7
#> 3 C        blocks            80          60             17.0            7
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_sed <dbl>, spatial_effective_dim <dbl>

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("SpATS", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spatial <- analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage(trial, "yield", stage1 = "spatial")
  spatial$locations
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   location stage1_model n_plots n_genotypes residual_variance residual_df
#>   <chr>    <chr>          <int>       <int>             <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 A        spatial           80          60              4.01        14.0
#> 2 B        spatial           80          60              2.79        12.0
#> 3 C        spatial           80          60             17.0         15.5
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_sed <dbl>, spatial_effective_dim <dbl>
# }
